So if you’re not checking you’d wind up following the majority chain whether it was right or not. Attestations for the wrong chain wouldn’t be included or gossiped by any validator that does check execution because you don’t process attestations you don’t have the block for. And you’d disconnect everyone that sends bad blocks which would isolate the bad chain network and any validators that don’t check. So I’d expect validators following the bad chain to do significantly worse even if they aren’t completely excluded. I’d say validators that don’t check execution would find they’re attesting for the right thing but have either no peers or that they’ve formed a third chain consisting only of validators who don’t check. I don't see it this way, consider the situation that happened today: I am a validator that doesn´t check anything and you are a validator that checks execution. We both run an old Geth. We see a bad block and we both attest to it. But chances are that the next block we see is a good one (specially when there is a strong majority). So we both receive a good block now, your client deems this block is bad, so it doesn't attest for it, it attest for his last bad block which is still going to get him banned fairly soon. My client attests for the good block. Now it may be up to the scoring system, but either way my client is doing better than yours. And in the worst case a winning strategy is still not to check and change peers If you’re running an old geth you’ll do worst of all. If you’re not checking you’ll do better but get lumped in with the bad nodes and booted. The people who run the latest geth and validate blocks should wind up doing best of all. It may not happen for the first few blocks but if you’re not validator you’ll gossip bad blocks and get disconnected from everyone validating the good chain. Yes you can find some new peers but you’re going to run out of them pretty fast. I don´t see which argument you are trying to make, what is the advantage of validating execution here? I am giving you a clear advantage of not doing so what ever happened with the eth1 vote? did we vote on the 'right' block or on the forked version? I’m saying that if you don’t validate and the majority or at least enough do you’ll wind up with no peers and effectively be offline in this situation because you’ll broadcast both the good and bad blocks and be disconnected. If there aren’t enough nodes validating then you can get away with it but then the network has no security and everything’s ruined. So you are saying that a non-checking validator will eventually be loosing money, and a checking validator is surely to lose money, ergo it's better to not check. There are plenty of situations where the game-theoretic strategy for the one does not work if every single person applies it. But nonetheless, this is one of those cases where following the specs not only costs you resources but actual money. I can't think of a good way of punishing this behavior, but I think this should be a punishable offense otherwise we're sure to see forks of clients that do not check execution and gossip the minimum possible No I’m saying checking validators will be the only nodes remaining on the correct chain. Or rather only checking clients with updated geth will be b That is not true, checking and non-checking validators in the good chain will remain Everyone else will broadcast bad blocks and be disconnected so wind up only following the bad chain. there is no advantage to checking Checking validators will disconnect non checking validators for gossiping bad blocks. Same as outdated geth nodes will no longer be connected to updated ones on eth1 yes but this does not matter to the point: can you show me an advantage to checking? Am I really talking nonsense or I just don't see where you are pointing to an advantage of checking The advantage to checking is that it’s the only way to stay connected to the network no If you don’t check you will gossip bad blocks and be disconnected. You will no longer be able to follow the correct chain. excuse me for barging into your convo, but what ever happened with the eth1 vote? that's the whole point: we have 4 kinds of validators in this scenario: Good geth checking, those guys are fine. Attestations for the wrong chain wouldn’t be included or gossiped by any validator that does check execution because you don’t process attestations you don’t have the block for. I’d say validators that don’t check execution would find they’re attesting for the right thing but have either no peers or that they’ve formed a third chain consisting only of validators who don’t check.

So we both receive a good block now, your client deems this block is bad, so it doesn't attest for it, it attest for his last bad block which is still going to get him banned fairly soon. My client attests for the good block. Now it may be up to the scoring system, but either way my client is doing better than yours.
